before.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; the exact algebraic identities are stated with their pointwise-regularity hypotheses; solvability is left to the reachability theorem
before.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval, $c>0$, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ ([[def-em-fields]]) and Lorenz divergence and wave operator $$G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi,\qquad W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta.$$ Let $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous sources ([[def-em-sources]]). (a) [Exact identities] Independently of any field equation, on $\Omega\times I$ $$\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+\nabla G.$$ Consequently the sourced Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold for $(E,B,\rho,J)$ if and only if $$W\varphi-\partial_tG=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad WA+\nabla G=\mu_0J\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$ (b) [Gauge shift] If $\chi$ is a gauge function of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$, then $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi$ on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]), and the transformed pair has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Hence $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge if and only if $W\chi=G$ on $\Omega\times I$. (c) [Decoupling] For this pair and sources, the pair is in Lorenz gauge and satisfies the two decoupled sourced wave equations $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$ if and only if its field pair solves the sourced Maxwell system on $\Omega\times I$ (the source-free pair $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ being automatic for a potential pair). Thus in Lorenz gauge the sourced Maxwell system is exactly a pair of decoupled wave equations, componentwise for $A$. (d) [Residual generators] If $W\chi=0$ then the transform of a pair in Lorenz gauge is again in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair; the Lorenz condition therefore does not determine the potential pair. (e) [Scope] The identities and equivalences are properties of a given potential representation of class $C^2$; they assert no existence of a generator with $W\chi=G$ (or with prescribed data), which is the subject of the gauge-reachability theorem on this page, and they impose no boundary, decay or initial condition. A pair of class $C^1$ defines $E,B$ but need not have the second derivatives appearing in $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\Delta$ or $\partial_tG$, so $C^2$ is the exact standing regularity here.

before.title: Energy flow in crossed external fields with finite-volume accounting
before.statement:
Let $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$, $E_0>0$, and on $\Omega\times I=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ define, with $\theta(x,t):=kz-\omega t$, the frame $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], and the encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]],
$$E(x,t):=E_0\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_1=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[E_0e_1e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr],\qquad B(x,t):=\frac{E_0}{c}\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_2=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\tfrac{E_0}{c}e_2e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr].$$
The electric and magnetic fields are perpendicular to one another and to the direction $e_3$ ('crossed' fields); $E$ oscillates along $e_1$, $B$ along $e_2$. Then:
(a) [Field data] $E$ and $B$ are smooth fields of [[def-em-fields]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, and they satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho=0$ and $J=0$.
(b) [Energy density and flux] With $u$ and $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]],
$$u(x,t)=\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t),\qquad S(x,t)=\varepsilon_0cE_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t)\,e_3,$$
and the local balance $\partial_tu+\partial_zS_3=0$, equivalently $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=0$, holds exactly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$.
(c) [Finite-volume accounting] For $a<b$, $L_1,L_2>0$ and the box $B:=(0,L_1)\times(0,L_2)\times(a,b)$ with outward normal $n$, for every $t$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{B}u\,dV=L_1L_2\bigl(S_3(a,t)-S_3(b,t)\bigr)=-\oint_{\partial B}S\cdot n\,dS:$$
the four faces with normals $\pm e_1,\pm e_2$ carry zero flux because $S$ is parallel to $e_3$, and the transverse faces carry the fluxes $-L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and $L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$.
(d) [Scope] The configuration is an ideal source-free plane wave, the finite-volume accounting of (c) is the fixed-volume energy balance of this declared solution in the sense of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]], and the example asserts nothing about the total energy of the field over all of $\mathbb R^3$ nor any empirical realization. $E_0>0$, $k>0$ and $\omega=ck$ are the declared parameters of the configuration.
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct substitution, with the oscillatory derivatives computed through the complex-exponential encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]. (a): the fields are of class $C^\infty$ because they are real parts of compositions of the linear map $(x,t)\mapsto i(kz-\omega t)$ with the entire exponential and of the real-linear projection, so the smooth calculus applies ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]); in particular, the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) applied to $\exp\circ(i(kz-\omega t))$, with the real total differentiability and derivative of the complex exponential ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]) and Euler's formula $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$ ([[thm-eulers-formula]]), gives $\partial_te^{i\theta}=-i\omega e^{i\theta}$, $\partial_ze^{i\theta}=ike^{i\theta}$ and, taking real parts, $\partial_t\cos\theta=\omega\sin\theta$, $\partial_z\cos\theta=-k\sin\theta$; substitution into the four smooth-branch equations verifies them with $\rho=0$, $J=0$ (both divergences vanish because the fields depend only on $z$ and have no $e_3$ component, curl $E=-\partial_tB$ and curl $B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$ reduce to the displayed scalar identities using $\omega=ck$). (b): $(E\times B)_3=\lvert E\rvert\lvert B\rvert=E_0^2c^{-1}\cos^2\theta$ by the orthogonal triad $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], and $\lvert E\rvert^2=E_0^2\cos^2\theta$, $\lvert B\rvert^2=E_0^2c^{-2}\cos^2\theta$; with $1/(\mu_0c^2)=\varepsilon_0$ and $1/(\mu_0c)=\varepsilon_0c$ from [[def-em-si-conventions]] this gives the displayed $u$ and $S$; the product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $\partial_tu=2\varepsilon_0E_0^2\omega\cos\theta\sin\theta$ and $\partial_zS_3=-2\varepsilon_0E_0^2k\cos\theta\sin\theta$, whose sum vanishes because $\omega=ck$; this is the local identity of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] for $J=0$. (c): $u$ is continuous and independent of $(x,y)$, so [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] reduces $\int_Bu\,dV$ to $L_1L_2\int_a^bu(z,t)\,dz$; [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates that integral under the integral sign; the local identity and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\frac{d}{dt}\int_Bu\,dV=-L_1L_2\int_a^b\partial_zS_3\,dz=-L_1L_2(S_3(b,t)-S_3(a,t))$; the evaluation of the six face integrals uses only that $S=S_3e_3$ is independent of $(x,y)$. (d) records the scope; no empirical premise is used.

after.title: Energy flow in crossed external fields with finite-volume accounting
after.statement:
Let $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$, $E_0>0$, and on $\Omega\times I=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ define, with $\theta(x,t):=kz-\omega t$, the frame $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], and the encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]],
$$E(x,t):=E_0\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_1=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[E_0e_1e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr],\qquad B(x,t):=\frac{E_0}{c}\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_2=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\tfrac{E_0}{c}e_2e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr].$$
The electric and magnetic fields are perpendicular to one another and to the direction $e_3$ ('crossed' fields); $E$ oscillates along $e_1$, $B$ along $e_2$. Then:
(a) [Field data] $E$ and $B$ are smooth fields of [[def-em-fields]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, and they satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho=0$ and $J=0$.
(b) [Energy density and flux] With $u$ and $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]],
$$u(x,t)=\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t),\qquad S(x,t)=\varepsilon_0cE_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t)\,e_3,$$
and the local balance $\partial_tu+\partial_zS_3=0$, equivalently $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=0$, holds exactly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$.
(c) [Finite-volume accounting] For $a<b$, $L_1,L_2>0$ and the box $B:=(0,L_1)\times(0,L_2)\times(a,b)$ with outward normal $n$, for every $t$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{B}u\,dV=L_1L_2\bigl(S_3(a,t)-S_3(b,t)\bigr)=-\oint_{\partial B}S\cdot n\,dS:$$
the four faces with normals $\pm e_1,\pm e_2$ carry zero flux because $S$ is parallel to $e_3$, and the upper face $z=b$ has outward flux $L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and the lower face $z=a$ has outward flux $-L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$. Their respective signed contributions to the field-energy change are $-L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and $L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$.
(d) [Scope] The configuration is an ideal source-free plane wave, the finite-volume accounting of (c) is the fixed-volume energy balance of this declared solution in the sense of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]], and the example asserts nothing about the total energy of the field over all of $\mathbb R^3$ nor any empirical realization. $E_0>0$, $k>0$ and $\omega=ck$ are the declared parameters of the configuration.
after.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct substitution, with the oscillatory derivatives computed through the complex-exponential encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]. (a): the fields are of class $C^\infty$ because they are real parts of compositions of the linear map $(x,t)\mapsto i(kz-\omega t)$ with the entire exponential and of the real-linear projection, so the smooth calculus applies ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]); in particular, the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) applied to $\exp\circ(i(kz-\omega t))$, with the real total differentiability and derivative of the complex exponential ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]) and Euler's formula $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$ ([[thm-eulers-formula]]), gives $\partial_te^{i\theta}=-i\omega e^{i\theta}$, $\partial_ze^{i\theta}=ike^{i\theta}$ and, taking real parts, $\partial_t\cos\theta=\omega\sin\theta$, $\partial_z\cos\theta=-k\sin\theta$; substitution into the four smooth-branch equations verifies them with $\rho=0$, $J=0$ (both divergences vanish because the fields depend only on $z$ and have no $e_3$ component, curl $E=-\partial_tB$ and curl $B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$ reduce to the displayed scalar identities using $\omega=ck$). (b): $(E\times B)_3=\lvert E\rvert\lvert B\rvert=E_0^2c^{-1}\cos^2\theta$ by the orthogonal triad $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], and $\lvert E\rvert^2=E_0^2\cos^2\theta$, $\lvert B\rvert^2=E_0^2c^{-2}\cos^2\theta$; with $1/(\mu_0c^2)=\varepsilon_0$ and $1/(\mu_0c)=\varepsilon_0c$ from [[def-em-si-conventions]] this gives the displayed $u$ and $S$; the product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $\partial_tu=2\varepsilon_0E_0^2\omega\cos\theta\sin\theta$ and $\partial_zS_3=-2\varepsilon_0cE_0^2k\cos\theta\sin\theta$, whose sum vanishes because $\omega=ck$; this is the local identity of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] for $J=0$. (c): $u$ is continuous and independent of $(x,y)$, so [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] reduces $\int_Bu\,dV$ to $L_1L_2\int_a^bu(z,t)\,dz$; [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates that integral under the integral sign; the local identity and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\frac{d}{dt}\int_Bu\,dV=-L_1L_2\int_a^b\partial_zS_3\,dz=-L_1L_2(S_3(b,t)-S_3(a,t))$; the evaluation of the six face integrals uses only that $S=S_3e_3$ is independent of $(x,y)$. (d) records the scope; no empirical premise is used.

before.title: Joint regularity of radial vector and scalar potentials on star-shaped domains
before.statement: Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped with centre $a$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let $k\ge1$, and let $B:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^k$ jointly with $\operatorname{div}B(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$. Then the radial witness $A(x,t):=\int_0^1s\,B(a+s(x-a),t)\times(x-a)\,ds$ is $C^k$ jointly on $U\times I$ and $\operatorname{curl}A(\cdot,t)=B(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$. If in addition $C:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ is $C^k$ jointly with $\operatorname{curl}C(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$, then the radial scalar witness $\phi(x,t):=\int_0^1\langle C(a+s(x-a),t),x-a\rangle\,ds$ is $C^k$ jointly on $U\times I$ and $\nabla\phi(\cdot,t)=-C(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$. For $C^\infty$ data both potentials are $C^\infty$ jointly. No global potential on an arbitrary open set is claimed.
before.strategy: Repeat the compact-rectangle parameter-differentiation argument for every derivative through order $k$; the parameter derivatives are continuous on the compact rectangle $[0,1]\times$-slices, so the radial witness is $C^k$ jointly. The scalar clause applies the published Poincaré lemma and its radial witness. On a ball the construction is local even when $U$ has holes; first and second cohomological obstructions must not be conflated.

after.title: Joint regularity of radial vector and scalar potentials on star-shaped domains
after.statement: Regularity convention for a possibly non-open parameter interval I: a map on $U\times I$ is jointly $C^k$ when it is the restriction of a $C^k$ map on some open neighbourhood $N\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ of $U\times I$; jointly $C^\infty$ means the restriction of one smooth map on such an open neighbourhood. For open I these are exactly the usual open-domain classes of def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms. At included endpoints of a nondegenerate time interval, time derivatives are the corresponding relative one-sided derivatives. For empty or singleton I the restriction convention still asserts extension existence and the stated spatial identities, but it does not determine time jets uniquely from the restricted values alone. This convention does not require a fixed uniform enlargement of an unbounded I. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped with centre $a$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let $k\ge1$, and let $B:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^k$ jointly with $\operatorname{div}B(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$. Then the radial witness $A(x,t):=\int_0^1s\,B(a+s(x-a),t)\times(x-a)\,ds$ is $C^k$ jointly on $U\times I$ and $\operatorname{curl}A(\cdot,t)=B(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$. If in addition $C:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ is $C^k$ jointly with $\operatorname{curl}C(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$, then the radial scalar witness $\phi(x,t):=-\int_0^1\langle C(a+s(x-a),t),x-a\rangle\,ds$ is $C^k$ jointly on $U\times I$ and $\nabla\phi(\cdot,t)=-C(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$. For $C^\infty$ data both potentials are $C^\infty$ jointly. No global potential on an arbitrary open set is claimed.
after.strategy:
The interval regularity convention is supplied explicitly in the statement, rather than treating the imported open-domain definition as already covering non-open products. To prove regularity in that same extension sense, choose an open-neighbourhood Ck extension of the data (intersect the extensions' neighbourhoods if both B and C are used). Let P be the set of (x,t) for which every (a+s(x-a),t), 0<=s<=1, lies in that open extension domain. It contains UxI by star-shapedness. It is open: at any one point of P its compact radial segment has a finite cover by balls contained in the extension domain; equivalently its distance from the closed complement is positive, and continuity of the radial map uniformly in s keeps all nearby (x,t) segments inside those balls. The identical radial integral of the extension data is therefore defined on P and is Ck there by the compact parameter proof below; its restriction is the stated potential. For smooth input use its one smooth extension and the same argument through every finite order. Curl-freeness/divergence-freeness is only needed on the original slices to establish the field identities there, not on the enlarged neighbourhood. Set w=x-a and z_s=a+sw. The spatial star-shaped hypothesis puts z_s in U for 0<=s<=1. For any compact spatial box Q contained in U and compact parameter subinterval J contained in I, the radial image of [0,1]xQ is compact inside U. Each component of the vector and scalar radial integrands is a finite sum of products of the polynomial factors s,w and the Ck components of B(z_s,t) or C(z_s,t). Chain and product rules give every mixed spatial/time word derivative through total order k as a continuous function of (s,x,t) on the corresponding compact product. Apply thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle in each parameter coordinate, with others fixed, and induct on derivative order. Uniform continuity on the compact product and lem-uniform-integral-error-bound show that each resulting derivative integral is jointly continuous. Included endpoints of nondegenerate time intervals use the relative endpoint derivatives of the compact-rectangle supplier. For empty or singleton I, construct the potentials using a chosen ambient extension on its open radial-admissibility set and restrict; this proves the same extension existence and spatial identities, without claiming uniquely determined time jets on the degenerate restriction. Thus both explicit integrals are jointly Ck, without assuming k+1 derivatives, and applying this for every k gives the smooth assertion. No surface-measure or Lebesgue integration/Choice branch of lem-em-parameter-integrals is needed: these are ordinary one-dimensional integrals in s on [0,1].

At each fixed t, the positive vector integral is exactly the witness of thm-a-divergence-free-c1-field-on-a-star-shaped-open-set-has-a-vector-potential, so curl A=B. For the scalar branch put Psi_C(x,t)=integral_0^1 <C(z_s,t),w> ds, and take phi_C=-Psi_C. The published Poincare theorem gives grad Psi_C=C; its convention is positive gradient, so it cannot itself justify grad of the positive integral being -C. Explicitly, curl C=0 means partial_j C_i=partial_i C_j in three dimensions. Differentiation gives partial_j Psi_C=integral_0^1 [C_j(z_s,t)+s sum_i w_i partial_j C_i(z_s,t)] ds. Replace partial_j C_i by partial_i C_j; the integrand becomes d/ds[s C_j(z_s,t)]. thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative gives C_j(x,t)-0*C_j(a,t)=C_j(x,t), hence partial_j phi_C=-C_j. Therefore grad phi_C=-C with the stated finite-k and smooth joint regularity. In particular for C=e1, phi_C=-(x1-a1), so grad phi_C=-e1; the old positive integral gave +e1 and was a concrete contradiction. Neither a general non-star-shaped global existence claim nor a new physical assumption is introduced. On a ball the same construction is local even when the surrounding open set has holes; scalar circulation and vector-flux obstructions remain distinct.

before.title: Smooth scalar and vector potentials on a star-shaped space-time region
before.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K7 and mathematical-prerequisites.md#M05; interfaces aligned to lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials and def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions

before.statement: Let $c>0$. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open set that is star-shaped with respect to a point $a\in\Omega$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]). Fix an integer $k\ge2$ and let $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be fields of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-em-fields]]) satisfying the two source-free Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on $\Omega\times I$ in their pointwise form $$\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,$$ with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Then there are a scalar potential $\varphi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly and a vector potential $A:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^k$ jointly ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]) with $$B=\operatorname{curl}A,\qquad E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$ If $E$ and $B$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$, then $\varphi$ and $A$ may be chosen of class $C^\infty$ jointly. Conversely, if $\varphi$ and $A$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$ are their field pair, then $(E,B)$ satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ on $\Omega\times I$. The theorem asserts existence on the stated star-shaped domain only: it claims no global potential on a general open $\Omega$, no boundary or decay condition on the potentials, and no uniqueness; potentials are auxiliary objects of the framework and not claimed to be observable.

before.title: Gauge reachability: Lorenz gauge on the all-space slab and Coulomb gauge on a bounded smooth domain, with residual freedom
before.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K7 and completed-expansion-arguments.md#W6; bounded-domain branch closed locally with the published elliptic resolvent and higher-order Dirichlet estimates
before.design_state: complete branch argument for the two declared branches; the older global gauge promise on bounded domains with prescribed data is outside the statement, as the design requires
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in branch (a) and the Axiom of Choice together with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as declared by its weak-solvability lemmas in branch (b) ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $c>0$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of the framework ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ and Lorenz divergence $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$. (a) [All-space slab; Lorenz gauge] Let $t_0<T$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ (the restriction of a $C^\infty$ pair on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ with $\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $W\chi=G$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$; the transformed pair $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, has the same field pair $(E,B)$, and any two such gauge functions differ by a solution of $W\chi=0$. This is the exact content of [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] read for potential pairs of the framework; its physical content is that every smooth potential representation of a field pair on a slab admits a Lorenz-gauge representative with zero gauge Cauchy data at $t_0$, without changing the fields. (b) [Bounded smooth domain; Coulomb gauge] Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $\bar\Omega\times\bar I$. Fix a smooth time-independent Dirichlet datum $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$. Then there is a gauge function $\psi$, of class $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $\bar\Omega\times\bar I$, with $\psi(\cdot,t)|_{\partial\Omega}=g$ for every $t\in I$, such that $$\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)(\cdot,t)=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega\text{ for every }t\in I;$$ the transformed pair $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge on $\Omega\times I$ and has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). The generator is unique among such generators with datum $g$; if $g=0$, then $\psi$ is the unique generator with zero boundary values. before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the Lebesgue-measure interface used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $g:U\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Suppose that $\int_Qg\,d\lambda_n=0$ for every closed axis-parallel cube $Q=\prod_{i<n}[a_i,a_i+\ell]$ with $\ell>0$ and $Q\subseteq U$, the integral being that of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. Then $g=0$ on $U$. In particular, for $n=2$, a continuous function on an open subset of the plane whose integral over every closed axis-parallel square contained in its domain vanishes is identically zero. The hypothesis requires all such cubes with every centre and every side length; a single cube or the cubes through one point do not suffice.

Hence $g(p)=0$ for every $p\in U$. The planar clause is the case $n=2$. No regularity beyond continuity, and no choice beyond $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is used.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $S\subset\Omega$ be a compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface in the sense of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], and let $a:S\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. after.title: Surface densities with vanishing test pairings vanish
after.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the surface-measure interface cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $S\subset\Omega$ be a compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface in the sense of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], and let $a:S\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. If $\int_Sa\psi\,dS=0$ for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]), then $a=0$ on $S$. Equivalently, if two continuous densities on $S$ pair equally against every test function, they are equal pointwise on $S$. The conclusion is pointwise and uses the continuity of $a$; a merely locally integrable density would satisfy only an almost-everywhere conclusion, which this statement does not claim.
after.strategy: Assume the stated Countable Choice convention. If $a(x_0)\ne0$, replace $a$ by $-a$ if needed and put $m=a(x_0)/2>0$. Continuity of $a$ on $S$ gives an ambient neighbourhood $N$ of $x_0$ on which $a\ge m$ on $S\cap N$. By the embedded $C^2$ hypothesis, the inverse/implicit-function suppliers give, after permuting coordinates, a graph chart $X(u)=(u,g(u))$ on an open $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ with $X(u_0)=x_0$ and $g\in C^2(D)$. Choose an open ambient chart neighbourhood $O\subset\Omega\cap N$ containing $x_0$, meeting $S$ only in this graph chart. Choose $0<r<R$ with $\overline B_R(x_0)\subset O$. The actual ambient bump supplied by [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]] is a function $\psi\in C_c^\infty(B_R(x_0))$, $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(x_0)$; extended by zero it is in $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ by [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]. There is no product-extension assertion for arbitrary planar tests. By continuity of $X$, choose a closed nondegenerate parameter square $C\subset D$ around $u_0$ with $X(C)\subset B_r(x_0)$. The graph density is $J_X=\sqrt{1+|\nabla g|^2}\ge1$ by [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]. The surface measure and restriction to Borel chart subsets are exactly those of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]; chart independence lets the integral of a function supported in $S\cap O$ be computed in this chart. Equivalently one may choose a compact Jordan region $C'\Subset D$, obtained as a finite union of closed parameter squares lying in $D$ and covering the compact parameter preimage of its support and use [[thm-surface-integrals-over-c-one-graphs]] followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] for the continuous graph integrand on $C'$. On the support of $\psi|_S$ we have $a\ge m$, and $\psi=1$ on $X(C)$. Consequently monotonicity gives $\int_S a\psi\,dS\ge m\int_{X(C)}1\,dS=m\int_C J_X\,d\lambda_2\ge m\lambda_2(C)>0$; [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]] gives $\lambda_2(C)=\ell^2>0$. This contradicts the given zero pairing. Every $x_0\in S$ therefore has $a(x_0)=0$, and applying this to the difference proves the equal-density clause. The compact embedded $C^2$ interface here is within the published compact embedded $C^1$ surface-measure class, with no change to its measure convention; in particular the closed stationary interfaces used by the jump theorem are covered. No new Choice principle is used. The empty-surface case is immediate.

before.title: Fixed volume and patch test geometries, outward normals and induced orientations
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention already carried by the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentations and by the compact $C^1$ surface measure cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ open and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ a nonempty open interval. This definition fixes the time-independent spatial test geometries of the integral form of the Maxwell equations.

(a) [Volume test geometry] A volume test geometry in $\Omega$ is a pair $(V,\nu_V)$ where $V\subseteq\Omega$ is a nonempty bounded open set with a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of its boundary ([[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]) and $\nu_V$ is the outward unit normal of that presentation off its edge set ([[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]). The closed-surface flux of a field $F$ continuous on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$ is the finite face sum
$$\oint_{\partial V}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS:=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS,$$
with the face surface integrals of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. Every axis-parallel closed box $V=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]$ with $a_i<b_i$ and $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$ carries its natural six-face presentation, whose faces are its two-dimensional faces with the outward normals $\pm e_i$; it is therefore a volume test geometry.

(b) [Patch test geometry] A patch test geometry in $\Omega$ is a regular $C^2$ surface patch $(D,r)$ over a finite elementary Green region in the sense of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]], [[def-admissible-regular-parametrized-surface-patch]]): $D\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ is a finite elementary Green region, $r$ is of class $C^2$ on an open neighbourhood of $D$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), $r_u\times r_v\ne0$ on the interior of $D$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) and no interior parameter point shares its image with a distinct point of $D$. Its induced boundary chain $\partial S=r(\partial D)$ and its circulation $\oint_{\partial S}F\cdot d\mathbf r$ for a field continuous on the image are those of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]); its oriented flux of a field $F$ continuous on the image is
$$\int_SF\cdot n_S\,dS:=\int_D(F\circ r)\cdot(r_u\times r_v)\,dudv,$$
the scalar Riemann integral of the continuous integrand on the compact Jordan parameter region, in the orientation induced by $r$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). The pair $(D,r)$ is part of the data. Every affine graph patch $r(u,v)=(u,v,\varphi(u,v))$ over an axis-parallel square $D=[c_1,c_1+\ell]\times[c_2,c_2+\ell]$ with $\ell>0$, whose graph lies in $\Omega$ with $\varphi$ affine (for instance constant), and more generally every affine regular patch over such a square, is a patch test geometry: the square is a finite elementary Green region, and $r$ is smooth and regular with $\varphi_u,\varphi_v$ constant.

(c) [Regularity convention] When an integral identity of this framework is asserted for a volume test geometry $V$, respectively for a patch test geometry $S$, with respect to a field $F$ of stated class $C^k$, it concerns fields defined and of class $C^k$ on an open neighbourhood of $\overline V$ in $\Omega$, respectively of the image $r[D]$ in $\Omega$; when the identity involves a time derivative of a flux, the field is defined with the stated regularity on a neighbourhood of that compact set times the compact time interval of the assertion. No regularity away from these neighbourhoods is asserted.

(d) [Conventions and scope] Test geometries are fixed spatial subsets of $\Omega$ and carry no motion. A patch's orientation is the one induced by its parametrization, and its induced boundary chain has the compatible orientation of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]], so that the classical Stokes theorem applies with a plus sign. The definition retains the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of the imported boundary and surface-measure definitions; it asserts no differential equation, no physical law and no existence of fields.
before.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition. Clause (a) composes the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation with its outward normal and the compact-hypersurface face integral; the box is verified as an instance by listing its six faces (each a compact subset of a regular $C^1$ hypersurface patch, namely a coordinate plane), its twelve edges and eight vertices as the edge set, and noting that the face-edge intersections have surface measure zero and that outside the edges the boundary is locally a coordinate $C^1$ graph with the box on one side. Clause (b) composes the $C^2$ patch over a finite elementary Green region with the induced boundary chain and the oriented patch flux; an affine graph over an axis-parallel square is verified as an instance because a rectangle is both a type $I$ and a type $II$ region with the natural elementary decomposition, so the square carries a finite elementary Green presentation. Clause (c) is a regularity convention recording that all integral identities of this page quantify over fields on neighbourhoods of the compact test sets, which is exactly the hypothesis class of the imported divergence and Stokes theorems. Clause (d) records the orientation and countability conventions and states explicitly that the definition introduces no physical law. Nothing here asserts that every bounded domain is admissible, that a disc is a legal parameter region, or that a physical test geometry is realised by an apparatus.

before.title: Smooth differential-integral equivalence for every admissible test geometry
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the imported piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure definitions ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $E,B$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ source fields of [[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$; and let $(V,\nu_V)$ and $(D,r)$ be the volume and patch test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]. Assume the fields are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ and that the additional derivatives appearing below exist and are continuous there; for instance $E,B$ jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ is sufficient.

(a) [Differential implies integral] If the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, then for every volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and every $t\in I$,
$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \oint_{\partial V}B(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=0,$$
and for every patch test geometry $(D,r)$ the flux functions $t\mapsto\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and $t\mapsto\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ are differentiable on $I$ and, for every $t\in I$,
$$\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=-\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS,\qquad \oint_{\partial S}B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\mu_0\int_SJ(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS+c^{-2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS.$$

(b) [Integral implies differential] Conversely, suppose the two volume identities of (a) hold for every volume test geometry and every $t\in I$, and that for every patch test geometry the two flux functions are differentiable on $I$ and the two patch identities of (a) hold for every $t\in I$. Then the four smooth-branch equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold pointwise on $\Omega\times I$:
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

before.title: Stationary-sheet jump conditions of the weak Maxwell equations
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the interface and surface-measure definitions cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and source fields of [[def-em-sources]].

Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density). Let $E,B$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with one-sided $C^1$ traces on $S$ at every $t\in I$, and let $\rho_v,J_v$ be continuous on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces of such a field $F$.

Suppose that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair
$$\rho=\rho_v+\rho_S,\qquad J=J_v+J_S,$$
where $(\rho_S,J_S)$ is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with densities $\sigma,K$ and the pairings there, in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e), and where the volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Then, pointwise on $S\times I$,
$$n\cdot[E]=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad n\times[B]=\mu_0K,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,$$
with the ordinary Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Equivalently, the surface current density is $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}\,n\times[B]$ and the surface charge density is $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot[E]$.

The theorem assumes a stationary interface: the hypersurface $S$ and its normal do not depend on $t$, so the one-sided $C^1$ traces also make $\partial_tE$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally integrable, contributing no delta terms. No magnetic surface charge or magnetic surface current is present in the sources, and correspondingly the last two identities assert the absence of magnetic sheet delta terms. A moving interface, a normal sheet current, or a sheet whose support changes with time is outside this statement and would require additional terms.
before.strategy:
Assume the fields of the statement. Because $S$ is stationary, the interface formula of [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] applies to the spatial divergence and curl of each field at each time, with the same normal convention $n$ from $\Omega_-$ to $\Omega_+$ and jump $[F]=F_+-F_-$ as fixed in [[def-em-surface-distribution]] and [[def-em-weak-sources]](c); in particular
$$\operatorname{div}E=\{\operatorname{div}E\}+n\cdot[E]\,\delta_{S\times I},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\{\operatorname{curl}B\}+n\times[B]\,\delta_{S\times I}$$
as distributions on $U$, where $\{\ \}$ denotes the locally integrable function equal to the classical divergence or curl on each open side, and $\delta_{S\times I}$ is the functional $\psi\mapsto\int_I\int_S\psi\,dS\,dt$ built from the sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c).

First separate the ordinary from the singular parts. Restrict the pairing of the weak Gauss law $\operatorname{div}E=\rho_v/\varepsilon_0+\rho_S/\varepsilon_0$ to test functions supported in $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$: the singular term vanishes, so $\int_{(\Omega\setminus S)\times I}(\{\operatorname{div}E\}-\rho_v/\varepsilon_0)\psi=0$ for every such test function. The function $g:=\{\operatorname{div}E\}-\rho_v/\varepsilon_0$ is continuous on the open set $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and its integral against every test function supported there vanishes; such a continuous $g$ vanishes identically, because if $g(p)\ne0$ one chooses a ball around $p$ on which $g$ has one sign with $|g|\ge|g(p)|/2$ and a nonnegative bump supported in it with positive integral ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]), contradicting the vanishing by [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] and [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]. Hence $\{\operatorname{div}E\}=\rho_v/\varepsilon_0$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$, and subtracting the resulting identity from the weak equation leaves
$$(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0)\,\delta_{S\times I}=0.$$
Testing with $\psi(x,t)=\varphi(x)\eta(t)$, $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$, and using that the inner integral is continuous in $t$ gives $\int_I\eta(t)\int_S\bigl(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0\bigr)\varphi\,dS\,dt=0$ for all $\eta$; the function $F(t):=\int_S(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0)\varphi\,dS$ is continuous on $I$, and a continuous function on an interval whose integral against every compactly supported test vanishes is identically zero, by the same one-dimensional sign-and-bump argument ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]); hence $F(t)=0$ for every $t\in I$, that is, $\int_S(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0)\varphi\,dS=0$ at every $t\in I$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); the surface density $n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ is continuous on the compact $S$ at each such $t$, so [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] gives $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ pointwise on $S\times I$. Repeating the same two-step argument — off-sheet vanishing by the sign-and-bump localization, then surface localization — with the other three weak equations:
- from $\operatorname{div}B=0$ (no volume magnetic source and no magnetic sheet term): $n\cdot[B]=0$ on $S\times I$;
- from $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$, whose right side is represented by the locally integrable function $-\partial_tB$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with no delta part because the interface is stationary and $B$ has one-sided $C^1$ traces: $n\times[E]=0$ on $S\times I$;
- from $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J_v+c^{-2}\partial_tE+\mu_0J_S$, where $J_S$ is the sheet functional with density $K$: $n\times[B]=\mu_0K$ on $S\times I$, which is exactly $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}n\times[B]$ since $n\times[B]$ is tangential.
All hypotheses used are those stated: the one-sided $C^1$ traces make the interface formula applicable ([[lem-em-interface-derivatives]]), continuity of $\rho_v,J_v$ on the open complement makes the sign-and-bump localization applicable there, and continuity of the traces and of $\sigma,K$ makes [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] applicable. The marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the convention of the interface and surface-measure items; no further choice is used.

before.title: Distributional Maxwell equations with point and stationary-sheet sources
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the surface-measure interface inherited from [[def-em-surface-distribution]] ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units and constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $\mathcal D'(U)$ be the space of distributions on $U$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]); recall that the pairing $\langle T,\psi\rangle$ is bilinear with no conjugation and that the distributional partial derivatives are $\langle\partial_\mu T,\psi\rangle=-\langle T,\partial_\mu\psi\rangle$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]).

(a) [Fields as distributions] Locally integrable fields and source densities on $U$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]).

(b) [Point sources] Let $I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $z:I_0\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$ is proper into the open set $U$, and let $q\in\mathbb R$ (coulombs). By [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]],
$$\langle\rho_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}\psi(z(t),t)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}z'(t)\,\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$ with $\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=0$. If instead $I_0=(a,b)$ has finite endpoints, $z$ extends continuously to $[a,b]$, the absolute improper integral $\int_a^b|z'(t)|\,dt$ is finite and both endpoint events lie in $U$, the same formulas define distributions with
$$\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$$
([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]); a finite-history point source therefore contributes an endpoint term unless that term is included explicitly, and the pairings above exclude it only by the stated properness or endpoint hypotheses.

(c) [Stationary-sheet sources] Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]], [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density; the sheet is stationary). Then
$$\langle\rho_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_S\sigma(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_SK(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$: for $\psi$ with compact support the inner integrals are continuous in $t$ on a compact parameter interval and the functionals are bounded by $(\sup|\sigma\psi|)\,\mathrm{area}(S)\,\mathrm{length}$ of the time projection of the support, and likewise in the vector case. A normal sheet current (one with $K\cdot n\ne0$), a line current and a moving sheet are not source types of this definition.

(d) [Field class] The fields admitted with singular sources are the locally integrable pairs $(E,B)$ on $U$, and, for the sheet case, the pairs that are $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with one-sided $C^1$ traces on $S$ for each $t$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]); for such a field $[F]:=F_+-F_-$ denotes the jump of the one-sided traces.

(e) [Weak Maxwell equations with a distributional source pair] Let $E,B$ be a field pair of class (d), let $\rho=\rho_v+\rho_s$ and $J=J_v+J_s$ be source distributions on $U$ whose volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are locally integrable volume fields of [[def-em-sources]] and whose singular parts $(\rho_s,J_s)$ are point sources as in (b) or stationary-sheet sources as in (c), and let $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Say that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair $(\rho,J)$ when, for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$, the four pairings
$$\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$$
all vanish, all derivatives being distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields and the source pairings being those of (b) and (c). This is the precise content of the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] extended to the point and stationary-sheet sources defined here.

(f) [Scope] No product of two distributions is formed anywhere: the fields occur only through their distributional derivatives paired with a test function, and the source densities $\sigma,K$ occur only inside the ordinary surface and time integrals of (b) and (c); products such as $\rho_sE$ or $J_s\times B$ are not defined by this item. The definition asserts no existence theorem for fields with singular sources, no conservation law (continuity for these sources is proved separately where used), and no regularisation. Sources that are not locally integrable and are not point or stationary-sheet sources, moving sheets, line currents, and arbitrary products of distributions are outside the definition.

Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants and units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $E,B$ be the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ the source fields of [[def-em-sources]], with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ on $\Omega\times I$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$, and suppose the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds with these fields and sources, in particular $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Then the continuity equation
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, where $\operatorname{div}$ is the divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and $\partial_t$ the partial time derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

(b) [Distributional branch] Let $E,B,\rho,J$ be distributions on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); in particular they may be locally integrable fields and sources identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Suppose the four equations
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$
hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$ with distributional derivatives. This includes the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and every distributional source pair, including source types defined by their own pairings, for which the four equations hold. Then
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$.

The conclusion is a compatibility condition: it does not assert that every source pair is compatible with the Maxwell equations, and by itself it proves no conservation of physical charge. No choice principle is used in this item.
before.strategy:
(a) Smooth branch. By [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] applied to the $C^2$ field $B$, $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$ pointwise. Taking the divergence of the displayed Amp\`ere equation and using linearity of the coordinate derivatives in the sum defining the divergence ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)$, and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] lets the two coordinate-derivative types be interchanged: $\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)=\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)$. The Gauss law of the smooth branch gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$, using $\rho$ of class $C^1$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Substituting, $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=\mu_0(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)$, because $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ by the definition $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\mu_0>0$; division by $\mu_0$ gives the claim.

(b) Distributional branch. Only the two pairings with $\operatorname{curl}B$ and with $\operatorname{div}E$ are used. By [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] the distributional derivatives commute, so for every test function $\psi$
$$\langle\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B),\psi\rangle=\sum_i\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_i\partial_jB_k,\psi\rangle=\sum_i\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_j\partial_iB_k,\psi\rangle=0$$
after reindexing $i\leftrightarrow j$ and using the antisymmetry of $\varepsilon_{ijk}$: the two expressions are negatives of each other. The weak Amp\`ere equation therefore gives $\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$, again by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] and linearity of the pairing ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). The weak Gauss law gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$; substituting and dividing as in (a) gives $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. Every step is either an identity for distributions or the definition of the distributional derivative applied to a constant multiple, so no choice principle and no convergence theorem is used. The statement does not claim that every source pair admits fields satisfying the four equations: it claims only that whenever they do, continuity follows.

before.title: Evolution preserves the Gauss constraints
before.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], $I$ an open interval ([[def-interval]]), with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the source fields of [[def-em-sources]]; put $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and define the two Gauss defects
$$D_B:=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad D_E:=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0$$
with the operators of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$, and suppose the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds. Then
$$\partial_tD_B=0,\qquad \partial_tD_E=0$$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$. Consequently, for every fixed $x\in\Omega$, the functions $t\mapsto D_B(x,t)$ and $t\mapsto D_E(x,t)$ are constant on the interval $I$: if the two Gauss constraints hold at one time $t_0\in I$, that is $D_B(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $D_E(\cdot,t_0)=0$, then they hold at every $t\in I$; and if a defect is nonzero at one time it is nonzero, with the same value, at every time.

(b) [Distributional branch] Let $E,B,\rho,J$ be locally integrable fields and sources identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and suppose the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds; let $D_B=\operatorname{div}B$ and $D_E=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0$ be the resulting distributions on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). Then
$$\partial_tD_B=0,\qquad \partial_tD_E=0$$
in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. Moreover, if $D_B$ and $D_E$ are represented by continuous functions on $\Omega\times I$, then those functions are independent of $t$ (this clause uses the Lebesgue-integral interface with its declared Countable Choice convention, [[def-countable-choice]]); hence a defect that vanishes at one time vanishes at every time, and a nonzero defect persists.

The theorem identifies the exact content of 'the evolution equations preserve the Gauss constraints': it is the combination of the divergence-of-curl identity with the continuity of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]], and it asserts no existence of fields and no measurement.
before.strategy:
(a) Smooth branch. Since $B$ is $C^2$, [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] gives $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}E)=0$ and $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$. Taking the divergence of Faraday's law and using linearity of the coordinate derivatives ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]) gives $\partial_t\operatorname{div}B=-\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}E)=0$, the interchange of the time and space derivatives being [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] applied to the $C^2$ components of $B$. For the electric defect, $\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)=-\operatorname{div}\partial_tE=\operatorname{div}\bigl(c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J\bigr)=-c^2\mu_0\operatorname{div}J$ using Amp\`ere's law and $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$; and $\partial_t(\rho/\varepsilon_0)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$ with $\rho$ of class $C^1$. Hence $\partial_tD_E=-c^2\mu_0\operatorname{div}J-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=-\varepsilon_0^{-1}(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)=0$, where $c^2\mu_0=\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ and the last equality is the continuity of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a). For fixed $x$, the functions $t\mapsto D_B(x,t)$ and $t\mapsto D_E(x,t)$ are differentiable on the interval $I$ with vanishing derivative, so [[cor-mean-value-theorem]] gives constancy on $I$, proving both the propagation and the persistence clause.

(b) Distributional branch. The same computations hold with distributional derivatives: [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] gives the commutation $\partial_t\partial_iB_i=\partial_i\partial_tB_i$ and the vanishing of $\sum_i\varepsilon_{ijk}\partial_i\partial_jB_k$ (the two reindexed sums are negatives of each other), and linearity of the pairing gives $\partial_tD_B=0$ and, with $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ and the distributional continuity of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b), $\partial_tD_E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. For the propagation clause, suppose $D_B$, say, is represented by a continuous function $h$ on $U$; then for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ the function $F(t):=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\varphi(x)\,d\lambda_3(x)$ is continuous on $I$, and for every $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ with $\int_I\eta=0$ the product $\psi:=\varphi\eta$ is the time derivative of the compactly supported function $\Psi(x,t):=\varphi(x)\int_{t_0}^t\eta$ ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]] supplies the bumps needed to write any such $\eta$; the construction is the standard vanishing-fibre-integral test), so $0=\langle\partial_th,\psi\rangle=-\int_I F\eta$. Choosing once and for all a bump $\beta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ with $\int_I\beta=1$, writing an arbitrary test $\eta$ as $\eta-(\int\eta)\beta+(\int\eta)\beta$ and applying the previous identity to the part with vanishing integral shows that the functional $\eta\mapsto\int_IF\eta$ is a constant multiple of $\int\eta$; hence $\int_I(F-C)\eta=0$ for all $\eta$ with $C:=\int_IF\beta$. The continuous function $F-C$ vanishes identically: if $F(t_0)\ne C$, take a subinterval on which $F-C$ has one sign with $|F-C|\ge|F(t_0)-C|/2$ and a nonnegative bump supported in it with positive integral ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]), contradicting the vanishing by [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] and [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]. As $\varphi$ was arbitrary, $h(\cdot,t_1)=h(\cdot,t_2)$ on $\Omega$ for all $t_1,t_2\in I$, by the same sign-and-bump argument applied in the spatial variable ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]). This proves independence of $t$, and the propagation and persistence clauses follow. The marked Countable Choice belongs only to this Lebesgue-integral localization clause; the algebraic parts of both branches are choice-free.

after.title: Evolution preserves the Gauss constraints
after.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with nonempty open time interval $I$ ([[def-interval]]), positive constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Define the Gauss defects
$$D_B:=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad D_E:=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0.$$
(a) Smooth evolution branch. Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^2$ fields and $\rho,J$ $C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]]. Assume only the two evolution equations
$$\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E,\qquad\partial_tE=c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J,$$
and, separately, source continuity $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. No Gauss constraint is assumed. Then $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ pointwise. For each fixed $x$, both defects are constant on $I$. Initial zero constraints at any $t_0\in I$ persist at every time; a nonzero defect at a point persists with the same value. Thus evolution and continuity cannot repair a nonzero initial Gauss defect.
(b) Distributional evolution branch. The same derivative conclusion holds for arbitrary scalar/vector distributions $E,B,\rho,J$ on $U$ satisfying the two evolution identities and, independently, continuity in $\mathcal D'(U)$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). This includes the original locally integrable field/source branch identified with regular distributions and the declared singular-source class when its equations hold. Thus $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ distributionally. If a defect has a continuous representative $h$ on $U$, assume Countable Choice for the indicated Lebesgue integral/localization interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); then $h(x,t)$ is independent of $t$. In this continuous-representative case its zero or nonzero value at a time persists. No restriction of an arbitrary distribution to a time slice is assumed.
(c) Full-Maxwell corollaries. Smooth solutions of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] satisfy the evolution and source-continuity hypotheses by [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a), and their Gauss defects are identically zero by the two Gauss equations. Its original locally-integrable weak branch has the same distributional conclusion. For admitted point/stationary-sheet models under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) supplies compatibility and the four identities again give zero defects. Conversely, in (a), or in (b) when both defects have continuous representatives, evolution plus continuity and zero Gauss defects at one time give all four Maxwell identities on $U$, pointwise in (a) and distributionally in (b).
This theorem is conditional on the stated equations and regularity. It proves no existence, matter dynamics, observation or empirical fact. The derivative algebra is choice-free; Countable Choice is confined to the continuous-representative localization and inherited declared singular-source formulation.
after.strategy:
(a) Smooth algebra. For $C^2$ fields, [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] give
$$\partial_tD_B=\operatorname{div}(\partial_tB)=-\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}E)=0,$$
and, with the positive commutation sign,
$$\partial_tD_E=\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=c^2\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)-c^2\mu_0\operatorname{div}J-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=-\varepsilon_0^{-1}(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)=0.$$
Here $c^2\mu_0=\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ and the final equality is the separately assumed continuity, not a consequence of the evolution equations alone. The coordinate operators and product/linear rules are [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. For fixed $x$, [[cor-mean-value-theorem]] on compact subintervals of $I$ proves constancy, propagation and nonzero persistence.
(b) The identical componentwise cancellation holds for distributions by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], whose derivative-commutation clause is choice-free: in $\sum_{i,j,k}\epsilon_{ijk}\partial_i\partial_jB_k$ the exchanged $i,j$ terms cancel. The two evolution identities and the independent continuity identity therefore give $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ without multiplying distributions.
For the continuous-representative conclusion, assume the stated Countable Choice and let $\partial_th=0$. Fix a spatial test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and put $F(t)=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\varphi(x)d\lambda_3(x)$. On any compact time subinterval the integrands have fixed compact spatial support and a uniform bound, by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]] and [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]]. Hence [[thm-dominated-convergence]] makes $F$ continuous. All products with compact temporal tests are absolutely integrable; [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]], [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]] and [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] identify their multiple integrals with $\int_I F\eta$.
If $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ has zero integral, extend it by zero and put $H(t):=\int_{-\infty}^t\eta(v)dv$. Equivalently start at a point strictly left of its support. The compact-test integral agrees with its Riemann integral by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], and [[thm-ftc-first-part]] gives $H\prime=\eta$. Since the total integral is zero, $H$ vanishes both left and right of the support interval; it is smooth and compactly supported inside $I$. Therefore $\Psi(x,t):=\varphi(x)H(t)$ is a legitimate compact test with $\partial_t\Psi=\varphi\eta$. Apply the derivative equation to THIS primitive test:
$$0=\langle\partial_th,\Psi\rangle=-\langle h,\partial_t\Psi\rangle=-\int_I F(t)\eta(t)dt.$$

before.title: A suddenly appearing point charge with zero current is inadmissible
before.statement:
Let $q\ne0$ be a real charge parameter (coulombs) and let $U:=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ with the laboratory conventions of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. Define a distribution $\rho$ on $U$ by
$$\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_0^\infty\psi(0,t)\,dt,\qquad \psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$$
— the point-source pairing of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) for the constant trajectory $z(t)=0$ on $I_0=(0,\infty)$, with the endpoint term omitted — and let $J:=0$ be the zero distribution. Then:

(a) $\partial_t\rho=q\,\delta_{(0,0)}$ and $\operatorname{div}J=0$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), hence $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=q\,\delta_{(0,0)}\ne0$ in $\mathcal D'(U)$: for every test function $\psi$, $\langle\partial_t\rho,\psi\rangle=-q\int_0^\infty\partial_t\psi(0,t)\,dt=q\,\psi(0,0)$, because $t\mapsto\psi(0,t)$ is smooth with compact support. (b) Consequently there are no locally integrable fields $E,B$ on $U$ satisfying the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair $(\rho,0)$ in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e): such fields would satisfy the distributional continuity identity of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b), which (a) contradicts. (c) The failure is exactly the omitted endpoint term of the point-source construction: by the endpoint clause of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]], the same trajectory on a bounded interval $I_0=(a,b)$ has $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$ with $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$. before.title: Surface independence of the total current flux and the role of the displacement term
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the test-geometry and divergence-theorem items cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-sources]] satisfying the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on a neighbourhood of the data below.

Suppose given two patch test geometries $(D,r_1)$, $(D,r_2)$ of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]] over the same finite elementary Green region $D$ whose induced boundary chains coincide as oriented paths (so both patches span the same closed loop $\gamma$), and suppose there is a bounded open region $V\subseteq\Omega$ with a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation whose boundary faces are exactly the two images $r_1[D]$, $r_2[D]$ with outward normals $-n_1$ and $+n_2$ respectively, where $n_i$ is the normal induced by $r_i$ (that is, $V$ is the region enclosed between the two patches; this is a hypothesis on the pair, part of its data). Then, for every $t\in I$:

(a) [Total current flux is surface independent]
$$\int_{S_1}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS=\int_{S_2}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\oint_\gamma B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r,$$
where $S_i=r_i[D]$ and the flux is that of [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]].

(b) [Conduction-only flux need not be] For every $t\in I$ the difference of the conduction fluxes equals the negative of the difference of the displacement fluxes:
$$\int_{S_1}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=-\varepsilon_0\left(\int_{S_1}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS\right).$$
Hence the conduction-only fluxes are equal exactly when the displacement fluxes are equal, and neither conclusion is forced by the Maxwell equations alone.

(c) [Explicit realisation] The following declared smooth data satisfies all the hypotheses above and has different conduction fluxes through the two surfaces. On $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$, fix $\chi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$, $\chi(z)=1$ for $z\le-1$ and $\chi(z)=0$ for $z\ge0$, and set
$$E(x,t):=\frac{t}{\varepsilon_0}\chi(z)\,e_z,\qquad B:=0,\qquad \rho(x,t):=t\,\chi'(z),\qquad J(x,t):=-\chi(z)\,e_z.$$
Then $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0=-\partial_tB$, $\operatorname{curl}B=0=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ (the last identity because $c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}=\mu_0$), and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. Take $D=[-1,1]^2$, let $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ with $0\le\eta\le1$, $\eta=1$ in a neighbourhood of the origin and $\eta=0$ on $\partial D$, and take the graphs
$$r_1(u,v):=(u,v,-2\eta(u,v)),\qquad r_2(u,v):=(u,v,0).$$
Both induced boundary chains are the square $\{(u,v,0):(u,v)\in\partial D\}$, the region $V=\{(u,v,w):-2\eta(u,v)<w<0\}$ is enclosed between the patches, and
$$\int_{S_1}J\cdot n_1\,dS=-\int_D\chi(-2\eta(u,v))\,dudv<0,\qquad \int_{S_2}J\cdot n_2\,dS=-\int_D\chi(0)\,dudv=0,$$
the first inequality because $\eta=1$ in a neighbourhood of the origin, so $\chi(-2\eta)=1$ on a nonempty open subset of $D$, whose area is positive.
while both total current fluxes in (a) vanish, consistently with the loop integral $\oint_\gamma B\cdot d\mathbf r=0$. In the standard charging-capacitor discussion the two spanning surfaces cut the conduction current in different ways and the difference is carried by the displacement term; the realisation above exhibits exactly this phenomenon in a self-contained smooth model. An idealised thin-wire current is not a source type of this framework and the capacitor interpretation is explanatory, not an additional empirical claim.
before.strategy: (a) Put $G:=J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE$, of class $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$. By the smooth Gauss law and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], $\operatorname{div}G=\operatorname{div}J+\varepsilon_0\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho=0$ on that neighbourhood, the last equality being continuity, [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a). [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] applied to $G$ on the specified presentation of $V$ — outward normal $-n_1$ on the face $S_1$ and $+n_2$ on the face $S_2$ — gives $0=\int_V\operatorname{div}G=\int_{S_2}G\cdot n_2-\int_{S_1}G\cdot n_1$, which is the first asserted equality. The equality with $(1/\mu_0)\oint_\gamma B\cdot d\mathbf r$ is Ampere's integral identity of [[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]](a) applied to either patch, whose induced boundary chain is $\gamma$; the two patches consequently give the same circulation. (b) Split $G$ in the equality of (a); this is algebra with the definitions of the fluxes ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]) and no further analytic input. (c) Verify the smooth equations for the displayed data by direct substitution: $\operatorname{div}E=(t/\varepsilon_0)\chi'(z)$ and $\operatorname{div}B=0$; $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}(E_z(z,t)e_z)=0$ because $E_z$ is independent of $x$ and $y$, so $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB=0$; $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ and $\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE=-\mu_0\chi(z)e_z+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\chi(z)e_z=0$ since $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$; and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=\chi'(z)-\chi'(z)=0$. The graphs $r_1,r_2$ are smooth patches of class $C^\infty$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] over the rectangle $D$ (a finite elementary Green region, [[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]]); since $\eta=0$ on $\partial D$, both induced boundary chains are the square at height zero ([[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]]). The enclosed region $V$ has the two graph faces as its boundary with the outward normals $-n_1$ and $+n_2$, and its presentation is the finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation required by the statement, with the seam over $\partial D$ as edge set. For the fluxes, $(F\circ r)\cdot(r_u\times r_v)$ with $r_u\times r_v=(-\varphi_u,-\varphi_v,1)$ gives $J\cdot n_i=-\chi(\varphi_i)$ for a graph $w=\varphi(u,v)$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]); with $\varphi_1=-2\eta$, $\varphi_2=0$ and $\chi$ as chosen, the second integral is zero because $\chi(0)=0$, and the first is strictly positive: $\eta=1$ on a ball $B(0,r)\subseteq D$, so $\chi(-2\eta)=1$ there, and the Riemann integral over the compact Jordan region $D$ of the nonnegative continuous integrand dominates $\lambda_2(B(0,r))>0$ after the Riemann-to-Lebesgue comparison ([[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]). The total fluxes both vanish because $G=J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE=-\chi(z)e_z+\chi(z)e_z=0$, consistent with the vanishing circulation of $B=0$. The bump $\eta$ is supplied by [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]]; the marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the convention of the test-geometry, surface-measure and divergence-theorem items, and no further choice is used.

Then $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0=-\partial_tB$, $\operatorname{curl}B=0=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ (the last identity because $c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}=\mu_0$), and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. Take $D=[-1,1]^2$ and its interior $D^\circ=(-1,1)^2$. Let $\sigma$ be the standard smooth step of [[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]] and define $h(s):=\sigma(2(1-s^2))$, $\eta(u,v):=h(u)h(v)$. Then $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, $0\le\eta\le1$, $\eta=1$ in a neighbourhood of the origin, $\eta>0$ at every point of $D^\circ$, and $\eta=0$ on $\partial D$ and outside $D$. Take the graphs
$$r_1(u,v):=(u,v,-2\eta(u,v)),\qquad r_2(u,v):=(u,v,0).$$
Both induced boundary chains are the square $\{(u,v,0):(u,v)\in\partial D\}$, the region $V=\{(u,v,w):(u,v)\in D^\circ,\ -2\eta(u,v)<w<0\}$ is enclosed between the patches, and
$$\int_{S_1}J\cdot n_1\,dS=-\int_D\chi(-2\eta(u,v))\,dudv<0,\qquad \int_{S_2}J\cdot n_2\,dS=-\int_D\chi(0)\,dudv=0,$$
the first inequality because $\eta=1$ in a neighbourhood of the origin, so $\chi(-2\eta)=1$ on a nonempty open subset of $D$, whose area is positive.
while both total current fluxes in (a) vanish, consistently with the loop integral $\oint_\gamma B\cdot d\mathbf r=0$. In the standard charging-capacitor discussion the two spanning surfaces cut the conduction current in different ways and the difference is carried by the displacement term; the realisation above exhibits exactly this phenomenon in a self-contained smooth model. An idealised thin-wire current is not a source type of this framework and the capacitor interpretation is explanatory, not an additional empirical claim.
after.strategy: (a) Put $G:=J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE$, of class $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$. By the smooth Gauss law and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], $\operatorname{div}G=\operatorname{div}J+\varepsilon_0\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho=0$ on that neighbourhood, the last equality being continuity, [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a).
